title: Tata Memorial Centre's IT systems lack policy and security controls, audit finds
dek: An audit of Tata Memorial Centre's computer systems found no approved IT policy, weak password controls, and missing data backup plans, leaving patient data vulnerable.
theme: IT security gaps in a public cancer hospital
indiaConnection: This audit examines how a public programme in India was carried out and recorded, and it states what the audited record can and cannot establish for the people in India who depend on it.

eventTime.label: Date not established in the supplied evidence

body.text: Tata Memorial Centre, a major cancer treatment institution, operated its computer systems without an approved IT policy, according to an audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India. The audit, which examined the centre's information technology management, found no IT Steering Committee to oversee software development. This meant there was no structured guidance for IT operations or security.

The centre also lacked a comprehensive data retention and archival policy. The audit noted that without such policies, the institution had no clear rules for how long to keep patient records or how to protect them. The absence of a formal governance structure is a documented finding, but the audit does not say whether this led to any specific data loss.

The audit reported that the centre's password rules were lax and its login checks were not strong enough. It was also observed that security reviews were not carried out on a regular basis. Because of these shortcomings, stopping online attacks and safeguarding confidential information such as patients' Aadhaar numbers proved challenging.

Cryptographic security was not maintained while storing passwords and Aadhaar numbers, the audit states. Additionally, there was no Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan. The audit does not provide evidence that any cyber-attack actually occurred, only that the conditions made such an attack more likely.

Across the Tata Memorial Centre's various locations, putting the Hospital Information System into operation ran into major holdups, and a number of its components stayed inactive. The audit also pointed out that no compulsory unique identifier existed for patients who registered, so it was possible for one person to be listed under several different registration numbers.

section.title: System implementation and patient data issues

body.text: When details of patients from other countries were entered, there were no checks to verify the information. Also, the Patient Scheme Management system offered no way to apply for a change in category. The Material Management System lacked proper follow-up and notification features, which led to a supply of medicines that had passed their expiry date. In addition, the Financial Management System was unable to produce key financial reports.

According to the audit, formal Service Level Agreements were never signed with the vendors. As a result, payments kept being made even though technical problems and system failures were still not sorted out. The audit does not mention how much money was paid or how long these issues lasted.

The audit's findings are based on its review of the centre's records and systems. It does not include independent testing of the security measures or interviews with patients. The record cannot establish whether any patient data was actually accessed by unauthorized persons, nor does it provide a timeline for when these deficiencies began.

statements.text: No approved IT policy existed at Tata Memorial Centre, and there was no IT Steering Committee to oversee software development.
statements.sourceScope: The audit report covers the centre's IT management practices as observed during the audit period.
statements.limits: The report does not specify when the policy was last reviewed or whether a draft policy existed.

statements.text: The centre lacked a comprehensive Data Retention and Archival Policy.
statements.sourceScope: The audit reviewed the centre's policies and procedures for data management.
statements.limits: It does not state what data was at risk or how long records were actually kept.

statements.text: The audit found that password controls were weak, authentication methods were not strong enough, and security audits were not performed regularly.
statements.sourceScope: The audit examined the centre's security controls and authentication practices.
statements.limits: It does not provide examples of any security incidents that occurred.

statements.text: Passwords and patients' Aadhaar numbers were stored without cryptographic security, and the centre also had no Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan.
statements.sourceScope: The audit assessed the storage and backup mechanisms for sensitive data.
statements.limits: It does not confirm whether any data was actually exposed or lost.

statements.text: The Hospital Information System faced significant delays, with several modules non-functional, and there was no mandatory unique patient identifier, leading to multiple registration numbers for a single patient.
statements.sourceScope: The audit reviewed the implementation and functionality of the Hospital Information System.
statements.limits: It does not quantify the delay or the number of patients affected.

statements.text: The Material Management System did not provide timely tracking or alerts, which resulted in expired medicines being kept in stock, and the Financial Management System failed to produce essential financial reports.
statements.sourceScope: The audit examined the material and financial management systems at the centre.
statements.limits: It does not specify the value of expired medicines or which financial reports were missing.

statements.text: Formal Service Level Agreements were not executed with vendors, so payments continued even though technical issues remained unresolved.
statements.sourceScope: The audit reviewed vendor contracts and payment records.
statements.limits: It does not state the amount paid or the duration of the unresolved issues.

statements.text: The audit's findings indicate that the centre's IT systems were vulnerable, but the record does not establish that any actual breach or data loss occurred.
statements.sourceScope: The audit report provides observations on system deficiencies but does not include evidence of exploitation.
statements.limits: It cannot rule out that breaches happened but were not detected.
